newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gas output dip may dent expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gas output dip may dent expansion plans.

text.p: Ukrainian natural gas production dipped this year compared to the same nine-month period of 1995, with industry officials predicting that the fall could damage government plans to increase output in coming years.
Volodymyr Maximov, a spokesman for state-owned Ukrgazprom, said his company extracted 10,730 billion cubic metres of gas for the first nine months of this year -- two per cent less than last year.

"Partly the reduction in output is linked to a fall in demand during the summer period, but it was also caused by a chronic failure on the part of our customers to pay bills, plus a lack of financing for the industry," he said.

A government programme due to be adopted later this month foresees an increase in domestic output from the current annual level of 18.2 billion cubic metres to 19 billion cubic metres by the year 2000.
Ukraine imports 66 billion cubic metres of gas from Russia and the Central Asian state of Turkmenistan and has huge debts to both nations.

"The government programme has good intentions but it is not backed by real actions," Maximov told Reuters. "We're not asking for assistance from the government. We're just saying leave us alone and remove all the obstacles for development of the gas industry."
Maximov said the gas exploration industry is taxed up to 63 per cent on its profits.
He added that the industry suffers from a chronic crisis of unpaid bills by industrial and private customers.
Last week the head of the Chernomorneftegaz company, which explores oil and gas on Ukraine's Black Sea coast, said his company stopped developing new drills due to a lack of financing.
Nikolai Ilnitsy, director of Chernomorneftegaz, was quoted by news agencies as saying that his company was also hit by unpaid bills. He said customers owe 99 million Ukrainian hryvnia ($56 million).

"We cannot increase gas output on the shelf. The situation with gas suplies is getting worse and serious," Ilnitsky was quoted as saying. "We are putting five times less gas into the winter reserves as we are supposed to do."
Ukraine's goverment recently ordered the industry to put five billion cubic metres of gas into storage for winter.
Gas is imported through local private traders, who sell it mostly to industrial customers.
